summary: A TypeScript MCP server that gives AI assistants such as Claude your own tools, run as a local stdio process.
description: Start a Model Context Protocol server in TypeScript on the official SDK. The starter has one tool that reads text files under a configured folder, with input and output schemas, a description written for the model, and errors the model can act on. The server runs over stdio, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other hosts start it as a local process, and its logs go to stderr so they never corrupt the protocol. Tests drive it through a real MCP client in memory and over stdio, and MCP Inspector lists the built server's tools. Replace the sample tool with your own; remote hosting over HTTP is a later decision.
seoDescription: A TypeScript Model Context Protocol server starter on the official SDK with stdio, zod tool schemas, MCP Inspector and Vitest client tests.

projectExamples.title: Team knowledge for a coding assistant
projectExamples.description: An illustrative server whose tools look up internal docs or runbooks so an assistant can quote them. Access to those sources and any credentials are yours to add.

projectExamples.title: Assistant tools for an internal service
projectExamples.description: An illustrative server that wraps a few calls to a company service as tools an assistant can run. Authentication, rate limits and write safeguards are your work.

plain.whatItIs: A starter for an MCP server: a small program that AI assistants such as Claude start on your computer to use tools you write.
